ctx.x: I had an office at 1674 Broadway. That's where I gave Willie 'the Lion' and James P. Johnson an office just to come and play...

Adam Clayton Powell...this was during the early days before he, you know, went into politics proper...There was a man in central Harlem named Joseph E. Ford. Joe Ford was my uncle. And, aside from having all these other good things happen to me, you know, getting jobs and making records and broadening my acquaintance with a lot of people...then when I find Uncle Joe, I find him in an NAACP boat ride I believe it was. They were giving an NAACP boat ride. And this man was standing down at 125th Street on the pier,…

Now, he had not heard from us from 1913 to 1937...'38. I said, "I am your sister's son." And he was a dark man. He turned snow white for a moment. And he was flabbergasted when he found out who I was and that it was real. It took me a moment to say, "Well now your father's name was Albert and your mother's name was Mary Jane.
